title: Retrieval quiz: communication, recruitment and training (2.1 to 2.3) and one 6-mark question
subject: Business
source: Written for business/y11 lesson 33 (Pupil PDF: 2.1 to 2.3 retrieval quiz and one 6-mark analyse question.)
intro: Answer from memory, then mark with the mark scheme.

questions.q: Give one example of internal and one of external communication.
questions.a: Internal: a staff meeting or email; external: an advert or a letter to a supplier
Any two: jargon, noise, information overload, language, poor choice of method
A document listing the tasks and responsibilities of a job
A list of the skills, qualifications and qualities needed by the person doing the job

questions.q: Give one advantage of internal recruitment.
questions.a: Cheaper and quicker; the person already knows the business

questions.q: Give one advantage of external recruitment.
questions.a: New ideas and a wider choice of candidates
Any two: interviews, tests, references, presentations
Training for new staff to introduce them to the business, its rules and their job

questions.q: Give one benefit of on-the-job training.
questions.a: Cheap and relevant: staff learn while working

questions.q: Give one drawback of off-the-job training.
questions.a: It costs more and staff are away from work

questions.q: A halal restaurant chain plans to train all its chefs in food safety off the job. Analyse the effects on the business. (6)
questions.a: Benefits: specialist trainers teach the latest hygiene rules, so fewer safety breaches and better inspection ratings, protecting reputation and sales. Costs: course fees and lost working time mean cover staff are needed, raising costs; trained chefs may leave for rivals. Level 3 (5-6): a balanced analysis with two developed chains of reasoning, both in context. Level 2 (3-4): developed reasoning, partly in context. Level 1 (1-2): points identified with little development.
